query: For the paper "Content-Based Table Retrieval for Web Queries" (arXiv: 1706.02427), answer this question: How are the tables extracted from the HTML?

Title: Content-Based Table Retrieval for Web Queries
Content-Based Table Retrieval for Web Queries Zhao Yan†∗, Duyu Tang‡ , Nan Duan‡ , Junwei Bao+∗, Yuanhua Lv§ , Ming Zhou‡ , Zhoujun Li† †Beihang University +Harbin Institute of Technology §Microsoft AI and Research, Sunnyvale CA, USA †{yanzhao, lizj}@buaa.edu.cn ‡§{dutang, nanduan, yuanhual, mingzhou}@microsoft.com Abstract Understanding the connections between unstructured text and semi-structured table arXiv:1706.02427v1 [cs.CL] 8 Jun 2017 is an important yet neglected problem in natural language processing.

[3] Source: 1706.02427.pdf | Page: 2 | Section: 2 Task Deﬁnition
Title: Content-Based Table Retrieval for Web Queries
A table t is a set of data elements arranged by vertical columns and horizontal rows. Formally, we deﬁne a table as a triple t = {headers, cells, caption} that con- sists of three aspects. A table could have multiple headers, each of which indicates the property of a column and could be used to identify a column. A table could have multiple cells, each of which is a unit where a row and a column intersects. A table could have a caption, which is typically an explanatory text about the table.

[4] Source: 1706.02427.pdf | Page: 5 | Section: 5.1 Dataset and Setting
Title: Content-Based Table Retrieval for Web Queries
We also conduct a synthetic experiment for ta- ble retrieval on WikiTableQuestions (Pasupat and Liang, 2015), which is a widely used dataset for table-based question answering. It contains 2,108 HTML tables extracted from Wikipedia.

[5] Source: 1706.02427.pdf | Page: 8 | Section: 6 Related Work
Title: Content-Based Table Retrieval for Web Queries
Venetis et al. (2011) go one step further and use labels and relationships extracted from the web. Pimplikar and Sarawagi (2012) fo- cus on the queries that describe table columns, and retrieve tables based on column mapping. There also exists table-related studies such as search- ing related tables from a table (Das Sarma et al., 2012), assembling a table from list in web page (Gupta and Sarawagi, 2009) and extracting tables using tabular structure from web page (Gatter- bauer et al., 2007).

[6] Source: 1706.02427.pdf | Page: 5 | Section: 5.1 Dataset and Setting
Title: Content-Based Table Retrieval for Web Queries
We select the tables occurred in the top ranked web page, and ask annotators to label whether a table is relevant to a query or not. In this way, we get 21,113 query-table pairs. In the real scenario of table retrieval, a system is required to ﬁnd a table from a huge collection of tables.

[7] Source: 1706.02427.pdf | Page: 1 | Section: None
Title: Content-Based Table Retrieval for Web Queries
In this work, we focus on content-based table retrieval. Given a query, the task is to ﬁnd the most relevant table from a collection of tables. Further progress towards improving this area requires powerful models of semantic matching and richer training and evalua- tion resources. To remedy this, we present a ranking based approach, and implement both carefully designed features and neu- ral network architectures to measure the relevance between a query and the con- tent of a table.

[8] Source: 1706.02427.pdf | Page: 8 | Section: 7 Conclusion
Title: Content-Based Table Retrieval for Web Queries
7 Conclusion In this paper, we give an empirical study of content-based table retrieval for web queries. We implement a feature-based approach and a neural network based approach, and release a new dataset consisting of web queries and web tables.

[9] Source: 1706.02427.pdf | Page: 2 | Section: 3 Approach Overview
Title: Content-Based Table Retrieval for Web Queries
To build a system with high ef- ﬁciency, we separate the task into two cascaded modules, including candidate table retrieval and table ranking. Candidate table retrieval aims to ﬁnd a small set of tables, such as 50 or 100. These candidate tables will be further used in the table ranking step, which uses more sophisticated fea- tures to measure the relevance between a query and a table. In the following subsections, we will give the work-ﬂow of candidate table retrieval and table ranking.

Title: Content-Based Table Retrieval for Web Queries
